--- title: "Random-intercept Gaussian ML scale validation and performance" jupyter: python3 --- phit's `fit_mixed_gaussian_intercept_matrix()`, R lme4 `lmer()`, and Python statsmodels `MixedLM` fit identical simulated observations with one random intercept, by marginal ML (not REML), with plug-in GLS fixed-effect inference. The [raw report](lmm-results.json) records versions, machine and thread settings, artifact and data hashes, and every measurement. ## Methods | Item | Setting | | --- | --- | | Workloads | 1,000, 100,000, and 1,000,000 rows with 3 fixed coefficients; 100,000 rows with 11 (counts include the intercept); min(100, n/20) groups | | Data | Simulated with NumPy seed `20261011` (see [Simulation and numerical checks](#simulation-and-numerical-checks)) | | Machine | Apple M5 Ultra, macOS 27, recorded 2026-10-11 | | Builds | phit release build; runtime versions are printed below | | Threads | Common BLAS and OpenMP thread variables set to 1 | | Repetitions | One untimed warm-up, then five timed fits per worker; workers run separately and alternate order | | Statistic | Median and minimum in-process wall-clock time | | Timed | One complete fit with every output materialized (see [Timing boundaries and methods](#timing-boundaries-and-methods)) | | Excluded | Startup, CSV parsing, data generation, and JSON serialization | | Memory | Peak RSS of the whole worker process | ## Recorded results ::: {#65dafe85 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} from pathlib import Path import json,sys import pandas as pd ROOT=next(p for p in [Path.cwd(),*Path.cwd().parents] if (p/'Cargo.toml').exists()) report=json.loads((ROOT/'docs/benchmarks/lmm-results.json').read_text()) assert report['model']=='lmm' print('Recorded:',report['recorded_at'],'Machine:',report['cpu'],report['platform']) print('Repeats:',report['repeats'],'Warm-ups:',report['warmups']) print('Tolerance policy:',report['tolerance']) def ordered_table(rows): table=pd.DataFrame(rows) table['implementation']=pd.Categorical(table['implementation'],categories=['R','statsmodels','PHP'],ordered=True) return table.sort_values(['observations','coefficients','implementation']).reset_index(drop=True) rows=[];memory=[] for case in report['cases']: assert case['agreement_passed'] for name,fit in case['implementations'].items(): rows.append(dict(observations=case['n'],coefficients=case['p'],groups=case['data']['n_groups'],implementation=name,version=fit['version'],median_fit_ms=1000*fit['median_fit_seconds'],minimum_fit_ms=1000*fit['min_fit_seconds'])) memory.append(dict(observations=case['n'],coefficients=case['p'],implementation=name,CSV_load_seconds=fit['load_seconds'],whole_process_seconds=fit['process_seconds'],peak_RSS_MiB=fit['peak_rss_bytes']/2**20 if fit['peak_rss_bytes'] else None)) display(ordered_table(rows)) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` Recorded: 2026-10-11T20:47:02.703831+00:00 Machine: Apple M5 Ultra macOS-27.0.1-arm64-arm-64bit-Mach-O Repeats: 5 Warm-ups: 1 Tolerance policy: {'absolute': 1e-07, 'relative': 1e-06, 'quantity_relative': {'covariance': 1e-05, 'std_errors': 1e-05, 'z_statistics': 1e-05, 'residual_variance': 1e-05, 'random_intercept_variance': 1e-05, 'sigma': 1e-05, 'icc': 1e-05, 'log_likelihood': 1e-09, 'aic': 1e-09}} ``` ::: ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display} ```{=html}

Download timing [SVG](figures/lmm-fit-time.svg)/[PNG](figures/lmm-fit-time.png) and memory [SVG](figures/lmm-memory.svg)/[PNG](figures/lmm-memory.png). ## Algorithm {#native-rust-optimization} phit follows lme4's penalized least-squares elimination. It separates within-group deviations from group means and caches an augmented QR square-root summary, so each trial variance ratio factors p + 1 + G rows rather than all n. Covariance is computed only for the selected solution. The [walkthrough](../notebooks/lmm-math.qmd#cache-a-square-root-reduction-following-the-lme4-idea) derives the reduction and checks its residual norms numerically. phit uses nalgebra QR and SVD with no BLAS, LAPACK, or sparse backend. lme4 uses a general sparse Cholesky factorization; phit's specialized reduction applies the same elimination and keeps SVD rank checks. ## Timing boundaries and methods Timed calls include estimation, fixed-effect covariance and normal Wald inference, variance components, ICC, likelihood/AIC, all population/conditional fits and both residual vectors, and all conditional group estimates. PHP also validates/copies inputs and converts all output arrays and group and sample metadata inside the timer. R uses lmer REML=FALSE with bobyqa rhoend=1e-10. Python uses MixedLM ML BFGS with gtol=1e-10 and recalculates plug-in GLS covariance to align with the documented convention. Its own joint observed-Hessian covariance is a different convention and is not compared. Rust scans a log-ratio profile grid and refines analytic-score roots with compact weighted SVD GLS fits, after a one-time QR reduction. The algorithms and stopping rules differ, so this compares complete API calls, not one common solver. ::: {#ba4f48bd .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} display(ordered_table(memory)) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display} ```{=html}

PHP's memory limit is disabled for these large nested arrays. Timer resolution, system activity, and caches can affect results; see the [OLS timing discussion](ols.qmd#timing-boundaries). ## Simulation and numerical checks NumPy RNG seed 20261011 generates correlated study hours and prior scores, independent standard-normal extra predictors, and schools with roughly equal sizes. Outcomes follow $$y_i=50+1.8\,\mathrm{hours}_i+0.2\,\mathrm{prior}_i +0.5\sum_j\mathrm{extra}_{ij}+b_{g(i)}+\epsilon_i, \quad b_g\sim N(0,6^2),\quad\epsilon_i\sim N(0,5^2).$$ This sample is separate from the saved small teaching dataset. Identical 17-significant-digit CSVs are used by every worker. All coefficient-level fields, variance components, ICC, likelihood/AIC and all group effects are checked. Observation-length outputs are fully materialized, but cross-runtime checks sample ten evenly spaced rows; small fixtures check every row. Benchmark absolute tolerance is 1e-7. Relative tolerance is 1e-6 for ordinary outputs, 1e-5 for covariance, SE, z-statistics, variance components, sigma and ICC, and 1e-9 for likelihood/AIC. Small saved references use the tighter uniform 1e-7 + 1e-6 × abs(reference) policy. At 100,000 rows, R's between-group variance differed from the analytic-score solution by about 2.6e-6 relative while log-likelihood differed by only about 8e-10. The log-ratio profile score was approximately 2.55e-4 in R, -1.88e-6 in Python and 3.12e-11 in Rust. A flat likelihood and the floating-point resolution of the objective limit how closely independently optimized variance components agree, and the variance-sensitive tolerances above reflect that measurement. Likelihood agreement keeps its tight tolerance. The finite profile grid is not a proof of global optimality. ::: {#5a234dcc .cell execution_count=4} ``` {.python .cell-code} display(ordered_table([dict(observations=case['n'],coefficients=case['p'],implementation=name, largest_absolute_difference_vs_R=max(errors.values())) for case in report['cases'] for name,errors in case['max_absolute_errors_vs_R'].items()])) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display} ```{=html}

Set matching `PHP` and `PHP_CONFIG`, and use `.so` on Linux. For a quick check that leaves the published report unchanged, add `--cases 1000:3 --repeats 2 --output .context/lmm-smoke.json`. A numerical failure aborts the run without writing results. See the [contract](../reference-models.qmd#gaussian-random-intercept-mixed-model) for model and inference limits.
